TASK 10: RESUMABLE PUBLISH UNITS.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, tests/test_publish_orchestrator_resume_fanout.py, tests/test_publishing.py. Never modify anything else (publishing.py/youtube.py provider adapters are FROZEN - wrap their existing calls).

BUILD (report design section 1 + the retry-policy table):
1. Split handle_publish into resumable units with stable IDs persisted in episode.json under publish_units: 'transistor', 'youtube_main_upload', 'youtube_main_visibility', 'youtube_short:<clip_key>' per approved clip, 'completion_readback', 'zernio:<stored per-post identity>' (consume the Phase-3 stored identities), 'promo_email:<stage>:<recipient>'. Each unit: {state: pending|in_progress|done|failed|terminal_ambiguous, attempts, next_attempt_at, last_error_class, receipt}.
2. _record_publish_failure(self, ep, reason, *, unit_id, retry_class, next_attempt_at) - per-unit failure, never whole-episode error for one unit (replace the current whole-episode attempt count ~:332-356).
3. Retry policy per side-effect class from the report table: Transistor pre-create steps retry 0m/+1m/+5m; at the create boundary ambiguity = terminal_ambiguous + review packet, never auto-create again; YouTube resumable upload resumes the SAME session (persist session URI/provider ID at first knowledge ~youtube adapter's return), response-loss with possible-created-video = terminal_ambiguous, never a second videos.insert; visibility/schedule by known ID retries +1m/+5m/+15m with readback after each; zernio per-post +1m/+5m/+15m missing keys only; guest emails per-recipient/per-stage with date-safe rendering at send time; solo episodes persist not_applicable: no_guests for email units.
4. Unify the persisted schema key to publish_expectation with a one-time migration read of legacy publish_expected (~:283-310; publish_reconcile.py reads the same object - do NOT edit publish_reconcile.py; keep the object shape it consumes).
5. handle_publish becomes a driver: iterate due units, honor next_attempt_at, stop on terminal_ambiguous with review, idempotent across invocations (a completed unit never re-executes - assert via receipt presence).

TESTS: unit-resume matrix - test_one_failed_unit_does_not_error_whole_episode, test_completed_units_never_reexecute_on_rerun, test_youtube_upload_never_reinserts_after_response_loss (fake adapter loses the response after returning a session marker -> terminal_ambiguous, zero second inserts), test_transistor_create_boundary_ambiguity_is_terminal, test_solo_email_units_marked_not_applicable, test_publish_expectation_migration_reads_legacy_key, test_next_attempt_at_honored (injected clock). TASK 11: READBACK PRODUCER (STANDALONE MODULE - orchestrator wiring happens in a LATER lane; build the module + tests only).

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/publish_readback.py (new), tests/test_publish_readback.py (new). Never modify anything else. Consume existing adapters READ-ONLY: publishing.py's Transistor GET paths, youtube.py's get_video_status, and plain HTTP GET for the site (requests) - your module performs GET/read-only operations exclusively, never create/upload/publish/patch.

BUILD (report design section 2):
1. read_transistor(provider_id, *, client=None) -> dict - GET the episode via the existing Transistor read path; return {provider_id, public_url, published: bool, title, episode_number, checked_at}.
2. read_youtube(video_id, *, client=None) -> dict - via get_video_status; return {video_id, privacy, publish_at, processed: bool, checked_at}.
3. read_site(expected_url, show_notes_hash, *, fetch=None) -> dict - GET the page; return {url, http_status, live: bool, notes_hash_match: bool|None, checked_at}.
4. refresh_publish_verification(episode_dir, now=None, *, transistor=None, youtube=None, fetch=None) -> dict - reads episode.json's publish_expectation + approved_clips + stored provider IDs, performs ONLY the readbacks whose IDs/urls exist, atomically persists the merged observations into episode.json publish_verification with fresh timestamps (temp+replace), returns the dict. Missing IDs produce absent observations (never fabricated), and a readback ERROR records {error} for that provider without destroying prior observations of OTHERS - but stale prior observations of the SAME provider are replaced by the error (freshness honesty).
5. Adoption safety: adopt_prestaged(episode_dir, candidate, ...) -> dict requires provider ID + exact episode-number/title match + exact approved schedule before writing any receipt; mismatch/unknown -> {'verdict': 'ambiguous'} and NO write.

TESTS (fakes for all IO): per-reader shape tests; refresh persists atomically (crash-sim leaves old file intact); partial-ID episodes only read what exists; provider error recorded without clobbering other providers; same-provider stale observation replaced; adoption exact-match writes / mismatch ambiguous no-write; module contains no mutating verbs (assert no attribute access to create/update/upload members on the fake clients).
